correctness.rationale: Finite bounded commutative BCK-algebras split into standard finite chain factors, and independent uniform sampling of each tuple induces independent uniform tuples in the factors; equation degrees therefore multiply. On the standard continuum, truncated subtraction is 1-Lipschitz for the sum of the two argument distances, so the real-valued difference of the two terms is L-Lipschitz in the sup norm, including repeated variables. A witness in C_(n₀) gives |t−s|≥1/(n₀−1). For Q=L(n₀−1) and δ=1/(4Q), a one-sided coordinate box of length δ at the witness stays in the cube and entirely violates the equation, even for boundary witnesses. If n−1≥8Q, each interval has at least (n−1)δ/2 grid points and thus at least a δ/4 fraction of C_n. If n−1<8Q, a nonzero failure fraction is at least n^(−k)≥(16Q)^(−k). The trivial algebra satisfies every equation; terms with no variables evaluate to 0 or 1 on nontrivial chains, and are either equal everywhere or fail entirely there. Consequently the dichotomy and bound hold. In the accompanying example a pair violates exactly when x>y>0, giving (n−1)(n−2)/2 failures, hence one at n=3 and the reported witness bound 1/25600. The frozen exact-arithmetic checker was inspected, not executed; its finite range is not used for the proof.

evidence: McNaughton functions give continuous integer piecewise-linear term functions and rational polyhedral loci. In particular any real counterexample has a neighborhood of counterexamples, so qualitative uniform eventual failure density follows readily using standard grid counting. The inspected representation does not give the stated explicit uniform witness/term-complexity bound or control the small failing chains.

The present argument sizes a box using the rational margin and the occurrence-count Lipschitz bound, then covers the sparse grids with the one-failure bound. It does not show that the maximum nonunit degree is attained, nor does it need that assertion.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Separate the elementary qualitative consequence of known structure and continuity from the supported quantitative contribution, which holds at every chain size with a single explicit constant and extends to products.

evidence: Bounded commutative BCK and MV are term-equivalent; finite-chain evaluation becomes Łukasiewicz term evaluation on equally spaced grids. So matching same-chain and MV formulations were treated as germane, not screened out by terminology.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Term-equivalence leads to the same question in MV language, while a chain ordered as a grid is not enough for equivalence if its operations are Gödel operations rather than truncated subtraction.

originality.rationale: The all-equation quantitative bound is distinct on the evidence inspected. Evans provides a conditional chain-gap criterion and examples, not a uniform quantitative grid estimate for arbitrary equations. The finite product theorem and McNaughton representation are established background. The closest indexed all-equation classification is for Gödel chains, and the closer same-chain indexed result is restricted to two identities.
residual_risks: The Cignoli–D’Ottaviano–Mundici book was identified via Evans but not inspected in full; access to McNaughton's original paper did not yield full text. The representation itself was independently confirmed in accessible primary text.
An unindexed or implicit equivalent in quantitative MV-logic, polyhedral counting or probability remains possible; no priority certification is claimed.

value.rationale: The result replaces a per-identity hypothesis about the set of chain degrees by a bound recoverable from just a single witness and the term syntax. It explains why no sequence of nonunit degrees can approach one in this class, for all arities, and is a useful contrast to Heyting or unrestricted BCK behavior. It does not claim a sharp gap.
